_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 directly to contract v3 (Boston pilot JSONs are structural ground truth; GROK-SPEC-archetype-templates-2026-08-15.md + ADDENDUM v3 define the contract). Sources: new-york/REVENUE-STACK-NEW-YORK.md + new-york/CREW-COST-NEW-YORK.md + new-york/hub.json (geometry, gates, locked seat bands, area). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. Fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6′ utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals. NY DEVIATIONS FROM BOSTON, all deliberate: (1) fleet_phasing OMITTED — REVENUE-STACK-NEW-YORK.md carries no per-line vessel counts; its nav anchor is omitted too (fail closed). (2) demand_pool renders cluster-level evidence only — hub.json gates set forbid_employer_names; no named-employer table exists for NY. (3) L1 renders in TWO seat bands ($650–750 ferry-alternative / $750–900 gap) per hub.json locked_numbers; revenue_build splits L1 into two rows per scenario so the blend is visible. (4) Conservative case is net-negative: payback renders '—' with neutral fn5; no scenario is hidden. (5) pnl.data.sensitivities is a NY-only block (the stack's two honest levers as lever cards) — new renderable, same field contract. (6) Overnight-cargo upside carries its $ figures so upside revenue_build rows sum exactly to the P&L gross (deviates from REVENUE-STACK §6 note 3 'qualitative only'; flagged for Jaideep in _internal.deviations). (7) No legacy 'asset' key — navier_intro carries all vessel specs.

fn1.text: Pricing and experience rates are benchmarked to New York operators' published 2025–26 fares. One commuter-pass comparator's published rates carry an older effective date and are used as context only.

fn2.text: Demand figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships. Ridership and fare figures are from operators' and the city's own published releases.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect posted and local harbor speed rules. Speed-rule relief appears only as a separately labeled upside, never in base cases. Precedent: an electric hydrofoil exemption on Stockholm's Route 89.

fn5.text: At conservative fills, monthly operating costs exceed revenue, so no payback period is shown. The conservative case is a deliberate stress test, not a plan; the mid case is the planning headline.

fn6.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published New York-area government wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026. Local ferry job postings pay materially less; that appears only as a labeled sensitivity, never in the base.

fn7.text: Spot-seat leg counts are derived from spare commute capacity — seats not sold as monthly bundles — times the stated fill rate (10–30%) at $30–45/leg fares. Figures rounded to whole legs.

fn8.text: Committed seats are priced in two bands: $650–750/seat-month on corridors where a public ferry alternative exists, $750–900 where none does. The modeled vessel carries both, blended 5 legs to 3 across its day.

fn_n30_exec.text: N30 executive economics are indicative platform figures (all-in cabin + F&B on a ~$1M vessel, one captain, fixed AM/PM slots plus wait buffer). Shoulder charters/experiences are additive. Not a quote — ops walkthrough required.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in ~15% of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day. Commuter bundles are the schedule spine; experiences, charters, spot seats and overnight lines buy down payback.

revenue_rows.note: A monthly pass in two bands — lower where a public ferry alternative exists, higher on corridors with no water alternative.

Near-dock slow zones are short here; relief matters mainly in Connecticut's long no-wake channels. Not counted anywhere in base economics.

_provenance.structure: utilization_stack (D6′ LOCKED 2026-08-15): committed bundles (two locked bands, blended) → spot seats → experiences & charters → upside lines (sponsorship, overnight cargo, speed-rule relief) → opex → network share → scenario payback. All figures verbatim from REVENUE-STACK-NEW-YORK.md §5 worked model; arithmetic re-verified 2026-08-16 (sums match exactly).
_provenance.seat_bands: hub.json locked_numbers (Jaideep 2026-08-15): $650–750/seat-month with ferry alternative; $750–900 without. Modeled vessel blends 5 parity legs + 3 gap legs per day; committed seats blended 62.5/37.5 (§3 blend math). Blended $/seat: $683 cons / $747 mid / $808 upside.
_provenance.opex_basis: Energy 4.1 kWh/nm @ $0.30 = $1.23/nm × 1,764/2,055/2,506 nm per scenario. Maintenance $82.5K/yr midpoint of unvalidated $65–100K N45 range. Crew $130/hr = 2026-drifted BLS OEWS NY metro mean × 1.4294 ECEC burden, rounded up (CREW-COST-NEW-YORK.md); posting check (Hornblower captain + NY Waterway deckhand) implies ~$73.49/hr loaded — rendered only as the fn6 sensitivity. Insurance+berth $7.7K/mo carried from Boston, not NY-sourced — flagged in renderable note as 'may run higher'.
_provenance.payback_summary: conservative net-negative (payback —, fn5 neutral); mid ~9.0 yr headline; upside ~3.2 yr. Honest reads from §5: NY mid ≠ Boston mid because blended L1 $747 is 68% of Boston's $1,100 and crew is 153% of Boston's $85. Sensitivities: crew-at-postings → ~6.0 yr; gap-weighted → ~8.2 yr; both → ~5.7 yr.
_provenance.sponsorship_basis: $200K/yr fleet-level placeholder (÷4 vessels ÷12 = $4,167/mo) — NYC precedent depth (Citi Bike system title, Barclays station $200K/yr, NYC Ferry naming-rights sale in market, value undisclosed). Above Boston's $150K on precedent depth; still ~1 station-naming deal.
_provenance.cargo_basis: $350/run × 16 nights carried from the Boston ruling; NYC existence proof: Blue Highways microfreight pilot Atlantic Basin → Pier 79 (both network stops), no public rate. Clean classes: medical/lab specimens (E 90th/E 34th medical-corridor stops), batch parcels, catering. Seafood remains rejected (cabin-fit ruling).
_provenance.seasonal_note: NY-S East End seasonal line (Quanta LR, $625/$645 legs per hub.json) is NOT in this model — different vessel class and season (REVENUE-STACK §5).

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the 7-city network is the residual-value story.
